reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it is news coverage of the Nepal earthquake describing emergency communication and information services such as Google Person Finder, Facebook Safety Check, and reduced calling rates from providers. The channel subscription language and channel-page imagery are ordinary audience engagement and publisher promotion, separate from the earthquake-response services discussed.

citations.quote: Nepal Earthquake | Tech Support From Google, Facebook, Viber
Seventy-two hours after a series of earthquakes shattered Nepal and parts of India, rescue teams are still looking for clues
Google has activated the Peoplegender platform which allows users to post and search for information about missing friends and relatives
While Facebook has started the Safety Check-In feature
meanwhile in India bhakthi airtel has offered free calls to Nepal for the next 30 hours

opening.argument: Judge, the practical takeaway is more than an earthquake update: it points viewers toward services offering an immediate benefit. Google’s platform lets users “post and search” for missing people, while Google Voice calls are presented as falling from 19 cents to 1 cent a minute. That pairs a valuable result with using a named service. The segment does not merely say help exists; it describes what a user can do to obtain it. The absence of an explicit registration or payment instruction limits the case, but it does not erase the participation pathway being promoted.

citations.quote: Google has activated the Peoplegender platform which allows users to post and search for information about missing friends and relatives
Google is also reducing the cost of calls made to Nepal through its Google Voice service from 19 Cents a minute to 1 Cent a minute.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The earthquake context is real, but context alone does not settle the segment’s function. The defense identifies reduced calling rates as news; those same rates are concrete incentives to use the named services. Calling the channel subscription ordinary publisher promotion also leaves the service-use invitation unaddressed. The question is whether the coverage steers participation, not whether it includes genuine reporting.

citations.quote: popular voice and messaging app vibe that has over 3 million users in the himalayan kingdom has turned off billing for users in nepal to landlines or mobile phones globally.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Describing how disaster-response services work is not a deceptive offer. The cited actions concern finding people and communicating after an earthquake; the report does not ask viewers to claim a reward, complete verification, or pay to unlock either service. It also reports several providers’ rates, consistent with a news comparison rather than a single solicitation.

citations.quote: The killer tremors have thrown communication links out of gear. Internet access has been restricted, while mobile phone connectivity is unreliable.
BSNL & MTNL are also offering calls to Nepal at local rates.

opening.argument: Judge, look at the combination of urgency and unusually cheap access. The report says communications are unreliable while rescue teams are still searching; it then highlights a drop from 19 cents to 1 cent per minute and a free-calling offer lasting only 30 hours. The description also supplies multiple channel links and asks viewers to subscribe. None of those details alone proves deception. Together, though, the crisis setting, time-limited free offer, and links merit scrutiny as a participation pitch rather than an entirely detached account.

citations.quote: Internet access has been restricted, while mobile phone connectivity is unreliable.
Google is also reducing the cost of calls made to Nepal through its Google Voice service from 19 Cents a minute to 1 Cent a minute.
meanwhile in India bhakthi airtel has offered free calls to Nepal for the next 30 hours
Subscribe Now To Our Network Channels :- ET Now : http://goo.gl/5XreUq Times Now : http://goo.gl/U9ibPb

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the subscription links as separate from the reporting, but that separation is an interpretation, not something the mere presence of earthquake coverage establishes. The opening also cites a free offer with a 30-hour window. A careful judge should consider how that deadline operates alongside crisis reporting and outbound links, even though the cited link text does not claim to activate the calling offer.

citations.quote: meanwhile in India bhakthi airtel has offered free calls to Nepal for the next 30 hours
Social Media Links :- Twitter - http://goo.gl/hA0vDt Facebook - http://goo.gl/5Lr4mC

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The links are explicitly presented as network-channel subscriptions and social media, not as a way to claim free calls. The 30-hour period describes a provider’s calling-rate policy during the earthquake response; no quoted instruction ties it to clicking a link or handing over anything. Urgency arising from the disaster is not evidence that the report created a deceptive deadline.

citations.quote: Subscribe Now To Our Network Channels :- ET Now : http://goo.gl/5XreUq Times Now : http://goo.gl/U9ibPb
Apart from the mammoth rehabilitation efforts, re-establishing communication links have emerged as a top priority area.

opening.argument: Judge, the news format also gives the featured services a demonstration. The video shows a Person Finder interface with choices to look for someone or provide information, followed by prominent calling-rate and safety-check graphics. Its narration explains that affected users can notify friends they are safe. Those are concrete ways to participate in the highlighted services, not just background facts about the earthquake. The reporting frame may make that steering feel incidental, but its repeated focus on free or cheaper access and usable service features supports reading the segment as promotional.

citations.quote: While Facebook has started the Safety Check-In feature, which allows users in affected areas to select a notification alerting friends on their network that they are safe.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense’s news reading explains why these services appear, but it does not fully account for showing a usable Person Finder interface and emphasizing specific offers on screen. The title names the technology companies, and the narration tells viewers what their features allow. Those choices can function as promotion even when placed inside genuine disaster coverage. The separate channel subscription is not the central concern here; the service-facing presentation is.

citations.quote: Nepal Earthquake | Tech Support From Google, Facebook, Viber
Google has activated the Peoplegender platform which allows users to post and search for information about missing friends and relatives

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Showing the interfaces helps explain emergency tools in a news report; it does not establish a scam or a deceptive claim pathway. The segment covers missing-person searches, safety notifications, and calling rates across several companies because disrupted communications are part of the earthquake story. Neither the cited frames nor the narration asks viewers to make a payment or follow an external claim process.
